scores.label: A
scores.note: All judged options are 0. Each is a gerund with no object, so it drops both 'power' and 'too much'. Options 1 (craving), 3 (desiring), 7 (yearning) and 8 (longing) become generic desire and lose the meaning. Option 2 (coveting) reads awkwardly with no object. Options 4 (seeking), 5 (hunting) and 6 (chasing) are ungrammatical in place and lose the meaning. Options 9 and 10 are duplicates and failed the code checks.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 2 (lust): on its own it reads as sexual desire, the wrong sense. Option 3 (desire): generic, drops power and excess. Option 6 (lustiness) means vigor, the wrong sense. Option 7 (dread) is the wrong meaning. Option 8 (foolishness) is the wrong meaning. Option 9 (obsession) and option 10 (excess) drop power and change the claim. Option 4 (ambition) is the strong pick, and the paragraph's own word, but it sits in fourth place.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Option 4 (desire): generic, loses power and excess. Option 5 (covet) is a verb, ungrammatical in place. Option 6 (lust): wrong sense when used alone. Options 7 (craving) and 8 (yearning) are generic desire and lose the meaning. Option 9 (covetous) is an adjective, ungrammatical in place. Covet, covetous and covetousness repeat the same root.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 3 (arrogance) and option 8 (hubris) mean pride, not wanting power. Option 4 (desire) and option 5 (passion) are generic and lose the meaning. Option 6 (will) and option 7 (drive) are neutral or positive and lose 'too much'. Option 9 (avarice) is greed for wealth, the wrong sense. Option 10 (lust): wrong sense when used alone. The best option comes first.

scores.note: Option 7 (ambitious) is an adjective, ungrammatical in place. Seven of the 10 options failed the code checks as multi-word phrases or duplicates, but the best option comes first.
